To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DEAD box RNA heliases unwind duplex RNA in a non-concerted, stepwise manner, and that this process is regulated by a number of accessory factors.

the DEAD box protein DbpA uses ATP to unwind duplex RNA and remodels RNA–protein complexes by using its conserved DEAD box domain and an accessory domain, the C-terminal domain, which is essential for unwinding and RNA binding, and that this protein is an ATP-dependent clamp.
the DEAD box protein Dbp5 is required for nuclear export of mRNP and that Dbp5 and the DEAD box protein Prp28 act together to remodel the spliceosome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function, and regulation of RNA helicases, with a particular emphasis on their role in gene expression and RNA interference.
the molecular mechanisms of DEAD box proteins and their regulation by accessory factors.

the molecular mechanisms of the DEAD box RNA unwinding and clamping proteins, and their regulation by auxiliary factors, with the aim to understand their role in RNA metabolism and in the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DEAD box proteins are the RNA helicases that are DEAD.
DEAD box proteins are RNA helicases, but not all DEAD box proteins are helicases.
the DEAD box proteins are the most versatile and fascinating helicases in the cell, and that the next decade will bring many new insights into their function and regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand how the DEAD box family of RNA helicases work.

the DEAD box family of proteins are highly versatile RNA helicases that use their ATPase activity for RNA unwinding, but can also use ATP to form nucleation centres that are important for the assembly of large RNA–protein complexes.
DEAD box proteins are not just RNA helicases but also ATP-dependent RNA clamping proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

DEAD box proteins have a common core structure that is highly conserved in sequence and structure, but that the accessory domains and their interactions with accessory proteins are the key to their diverse functions.
the DEAD box proteins have been conserved throughout evolution and are likely to be involved in the regulation of many RNA–RNA interactions.
DEAD box proteins can be divided into two groups based on their ability to bind RNA.
